Six days ago, Apple released the first developer beta of iOS 27.2, skipping the iOS 27.1 beta. After releasing the second developer beta yesterday, Apple has now launched the first public beta of iOS 27.2, which includes a brand-new iPhone Health app. Apple has also enabled the ability to book and pay for lab tests through Quest Diagnostics within the new Health app.

iOS 27.2 beta includes a brand-new Health app and more features

iOS 27.2 is the version following the official release of iOS 27 on September 14. iOS 27.1 is designed specifically for the iPhone Duo.

Apple has detailed how the iOS 27.1 SDK lets developers take full advantage of the iPhone Duo display. You can see here how apps appear on the iPhone Duo, depending on which version of iOS they target.

Apple released Xcode 27.1 beta on Friday, adding an iPhone Duo simulator along with app development support for this brand-new foldable iPhone.

The first developer beta of iOS 27.2 includes the following changes:

  • The redesigned Health app, first announced by Apple at the iPhone 18 Pro launch event, is now available in this beta version.
  • Group FaceTime has been added to dual-lens shooting mode.
  • Siri AI language support now includes French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish.
  • Apple TV app profile features arrive on iPhone.
  • In Apple Podcasts, 'Up Next' is now renamed 'Latest Episodes'. The 'Continue Playing' section now appears directly below 'Latest Episodes'. The episode list in Podcasts also features a background that complements the theme colour.
  • Apple Music now uses less icon colour to indicate category labels within the app.

iOS 27.2 is expected to be officially released in October. iPhone users can currently get an early look at the new Apple Health app through the developer beta or public beta channels.
